Hypothesis: A conventional DNN will provide a reference point but may favour the overwhelming legitimate class.
Observation: At the 0.50 threshold, the baseline DNN achieved 99.9345% validation accuracy, but recall was 69.70%. It detected 46 of 66 fraudulent transactions while missing 20 (30.30% of fraud cases). Precision was 88.46%, F1 was 0.7797 and PR-AUC was 0.8166. The very high accuracy therefore overstated the model's effectiveness for fraud detection.
Decision: Retain E0 as the untreated baseline. Proceed to cost-sensitive learning to investigate whether fraud recall can be improved without an unacceptable increase in false-positive alerts.

Change: Introduced balanced class weights; architecture unchanged
Hypothesis: Increasing the training cost of fraud-class errors should improve fraud recall compared with the untreated E0 baseline.
Observation: Recall increased from 69.70% to 84.85% and false negatives fell from 20 to 10. However, false positives increased from 6 to 123, reducing precision from 88.46% to 31.28%. F1 declined from 0.7797 to 0.4571 and PR-AUC declined from 0.8166 to 0.7296.
Decision: Do not select E1 as the current preferred configuration at the 0.50 threshold. The improvement in fraud detection was offset by excessive false-positive alerts. Proceed to SMOTE for comparison with an alternative imbalance strategy.

Change: Applied SMOTE exclusively to the standardised training subset; DNN architecture unchanged.
Hypothesis: Synthetic minority oversampling should improve fraud recall while potentially producing a better precision-recall trade-off than balanced class weighting.
Observation: SMOTE increased fraud recall from 69.70% in E0 to 78.79% and reduced false negatives from 20 to 14. However, false positives increased from 6 to 50 and precision decreased from 88.46% to 50.98%. E2 achieved F1=0.6190 and PR-AUC=0.7910. This was more balanced than E1 but remained inferior to E0 on both F1 and PR-AUC at the 0.50 threshold.
Decision: Retain E2 as evidence that SMOTE improves minority-class sensitivity but do not select it as the current preferred configuration. E0 remains the strongest overall baseline.

Change: Replaced StandardScaler with RobustScaler while retaining the E0 architecture and no imbalance treatment.
Hypothesis: RobustScaler may improve performance because the transaction amount feature contains substantial skewness and extreme values.
Observation: RobustScaler produced modest but consistent improvements over E0. Precision increased from 88.46% to 92.16%, recall from 69.70% to 71.21%, F1 from 0.7797 to 0.8034 and PR-AUC from 0.8166 to 0.8186. False positives decreased from 6 to 4 and false negatives from 20 to 19.
Decision: Select RobustScaler as the preferred preprocessing method for subsequent experiments because it improved the overall precision-recall balance without increasing classification errors.

Change: Expanded the DNN to 128-64-32 hidden units and introduced Batch Normalisation and Dropout while retaining RobustScaler.
Hypothesis: Greater network capacity combined with regularisation may improve minority-class generalisation and PR-AUC.
Observation: E4 increased recall from 71.21% to 75.76%, reduced false negatives from 19 to 16 and increased PR-AUC from 0.8186 to 0.8343. F1 increased slightly from 0.8034 to 0.8065. However, precision decreased from 92.16% to 86.21% and false positives increased from 4 to 8.
Decision: Retain E4 as the current preferred architecture because it achieved the strongest PR-AUC so far and improved fraud recall. The precision-recall trade-off will be reconsidered during decision-threshold optimisation.

Change: Retained the E4 architecture and RobustScaler while introducing ReduceLROnPlateau, increasing the maximum training duration from 30 to 40 epochs and increasing EarlyStopping patience from 5 to 7 epochs.
Hypothesis: Adaptive learning-rate reduction combined with a more flexible training schedule may allow finer optimisation after validation loss plateaus and improve generalisation.
Observation: E5 improved precision from 86.21% to 87.93%, recall from 75.76% to 77.27%, F1 from 0.8065 to 0.8226 and PR-AUC from 0.8343 to 0.8432. False positives decreased from 8 to 7 and false negatives from 16 to 15. Training stopped at epoch 38 and restored weights from epoch 31.
Decision: Select E5 as the final candidate configuration before decision-threshold optimisation because the combined adaptive learning-rate and training-schedule refinement achieved the strongest overall validation precision-recall performance.
